In no event shall * Motadata be held liable for any damages arising from the use * of this software. * * For inquiries, contact: engg@motadata.com * */ /** * The Streaming package provides real-time data streaming capabilities for the Motadata platform. *

* This package contains components that work together to enable live data streaming for various types of information: *

* Core Streaming Components: *

    *
  • {@link com.mindarray.streaming.StreamingEngine} - Manages streaming sessions and routes streaming events
    • *
  • {@link com.mindarray.streaming.StreamingBroadcaster} - Broadcasts streaming data to connected clients
    • *
*

* Supported Streaming Types: *

    *
  • Log Tail - Streams log messages in real-time
    • *
  • Trap Tail - Streams SNMP trap messages as they arrive
    • *
  • Event Tracker - Streams event tracking information
    • *
  • Event Engine Stats - Streams statistics from the event processing engine
    • *
*

* The streaming package uses Vert.x event bus for communication between components and implements * session management to control the number of active streaming sessions. It also provides filtering * capabilities to allow clients to receive only the data they are interested in. *

* Streaming sessions are automatically terminated after a configurable timeout period if they * become inactive, and the system enforces limits on the maximum number of concurrent streaming * sessions to prevent resource exhaustion. *

* This package is designed to be scalable and efficient, capable of handling multiple concurrent * streaming sessions while maintaining low latency for real-time data delivery. */ package com.mindarray.streaming;

In no event shall * Motadata be held liable for any damages arising from the use * of this software. * * For inquiries, contact: engg@motadata.com * */ /** * The visualization package provides a comprehensive framework for data visualization in the Motadata application. *

* This package contains classes that handle the processing, transformation, and presentation of various types of * monitoring data for visualization purposes. It serves as the bridge between raw data collected from monitored * systems and the visual representations displayed to users in the UI. *

* Key components of this package include: *

    *
  • VisualizationManager: The main entry point for visualization requests, coordinating the processing * of visualization queries and dispatching them to appropriate handlers.
    • *
  • VisualizationMetricManager: Handles metric data visualization, processing time-series data * for charts, gauges, and other metric visualizations.
    • *
  • VisualizationEventManager: Manages event data visualization, processing event logs and * alerts for display in event-based visualizations.
    • *
  • VisualizationAvailabilityManager: Processes availability data for visualization, showing * uptime/downtime statistics and status information.
    • *
  • VisualizationComplianceManager: Handles compliance data visualization, showing policy * compliance status and statistics.
    • *
  • VisualizationNetRouteManager: Manages network route visualization data, showing network * topology and path information.
    • *
  • VisualizationCacheEngine: Provides caching capabilities for visualization data to improve * performance for frequently accessed visualizations.
    • *
  • VisualizationConstants: Defines constants, enums, and utility methods used throughout * the visualization system.
    • *
  • VisualizationQueryHelper: Provides helper methods for constructing and executing * visualization queries.
    • *
  • VisualizationEventHistoryManager: Manages historical event data for visualization, * providing access to past events for analysis and reporting.
    • *
  • VisualizationEventHistoryResponseProcessor: Processes responses from event history * queries and formats them for visualization.
    • *
  • VisualizationEventResponseProcessor: Processes responses from event queries and * formats them for visualization.
    • *
  • VisualizationMetricResponseProcessor: Processes responses from metric queries and * formats them for visualization.
    • *
  • VisualizationRUMHistoryManager: Manages RUM (Real User Monitoring) history data * for visualization, handling session and event history queries.
    • *
  • VisualizationRUMHistoryResponseProcessor: Processes responses from RUM history * queries, aggregating session data and formatting for visualization.
    • *
  • VisualizationTraceHistoryManager: Manages trace history data for visualization, * providing access to distributed tracing information.
    • *
  • VisualizationTraceHistoryResponseProcessor: Processes responses from trace history * queries and formats them for visualization.
    • *
*

* The visualization package implements a Vert.x-based architecture, with most components extending * AbstractVerticle to provide asynchronous, non-blocking processing of visualization requests. It * communicates with other system components through the Vert.x event bus. *

* Data flow in the visualization system typically follows these steps: *

    *
  1. A visualization request is received by VisualizationManager
    2. *
  2. The request is analyzed to determine the type of visualization and data needed
    3. *
  3. The request is dispatched to the appropriate specialized manager (Metric, Event, etc.)
    4. *
  4. The specialized manager retrieves and processes the required data
    5. *
  5. The processed data is formatted according to the visualization type
    6. *
  6. The formatted data is returned to the requester for display
    7. *
*

* This package supports various visualization types including: *

    *
  • Charts: Line, bar, area, and pie charts for time-series and categorical data
    • *
  • Gauges: Visual indicators for single metric values with thresholds
    • *
  • Grids: Tabular displays of data with sorting and filtering capabilities
    • *
  • Histograms: Distribution visualizations for frequency analysis
    • *
  • Top-N Charts: Ranked displays of entities based on metric values
    • *
  • Status Displays: Visual representations of entity status and health
    • *
*

* The visualization package interacts with several other system components: *

    *
  • Datastore: For retrieving historical and current monitoring data
    • *
  • Cache: For storing and retrieving frequently accessed visualization results
    • *
  • Event Bus: For communication with other system components
    • *
  • User Interface: For displaying visualization results to users
    • *
  • Configuration: For retrieving visualization settings and preferences
    • *
*

* Performance considerations in the visualization package include: *

    *
  • Caching of visualization results to reduce database load
    • *
  • Query optimization for large datasets
    • *
  • Asynchronous processing to maintain UI responsiveness
    • *
  • Data aggregation to reduce network traffic and processing time
    • *
  • Query timeout handling to prevent resource exhaustion
    • *
* * @see com.mindarray.visualization.VisualizationManager * @see com.mindarray.visualization.VisualizationConstants * @since 1.0 */ package com.mindarray.visualization;

* The aiops package is designed to reduce alert noise, improve incident response times, * and provide better visibility into complex IT environments by understanding the * relationships between components and intelligently correlating events. * * @since 1.0 */ package com.mindarray.aiops;

import json
import logging
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
import os

# CONFIG
INPUT_FILE = "/home/harshil/Harshil-PoCs/Dataset-Generation/enriched_production_prs.jsonl"
OUTPUT_FILE = "/home/harshil/Harshil-PoCs/Dataset-Generation/enriched_with_reasoning.jsonl"
MODEL_PATH = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct" # Ensure this path is correct on H100

def synthesize():
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    
    if not os.path.exists(INPUT_FILE):
        logging.error(f"File not found: {INPUT_FILE}")
        return

    # 1. Load Data
    logging.info(f"Loading {INPUT_FILE}...")
    with open(INPUT_FILE, 'r') as f:
        data = [json.loads(line) for line in f]
    
    logging.info(f"Loaded {len(data)} commits. Preparing prompts...")

    # 2. Build Prompts
    prompts = []
    valid_indices = []

    for i, entry in enumerate(data):
        instruction = entry.get('instruction', '')
        files = entry.get('files', [])
        
        # Heuristic: Use the diff of the first file to generate the plan
        # (Reasoning usually applies to the whole PR, not just file-by-file)
        if not files: 
            continue
            
        diff_context = files[0].get('diff', '')[:6000] # Fit in context
        
        prompt = f"""<|im_start|>system
You are a Senior Software Architect. Analyze the instruction and the code diff. 
Explain the reasoning for this change.
<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
Instruction: {instruction}

Diff:
{diff_context}

Provide a concise, step-by-step implementation plan and reasoning. Start with "Here is the plan:".
<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
"""
        prompts.append(prompt)
        valid_indices.append(i)

    # 3. Generate with vLLM
    logging.info(f"Starting vLLM Inference on {len(prompts)} items...")
    
    # Adjust tensor_parallel_size if using multiple GPUs (e.g., 2, 4, 8)
    llm = LLM(model=MODEL_PATH, tensor_parallel_size=1) 
    
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.7, max_tokens=512)
    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, params)

    # 4. Save Results
    logging.info("Saving results...")
    with open(OUTPUT_FILE, 'w') as f:
        for j, output in enumerate(outputs):
            original_idx = valid_indices[j]
            entry = data[original_idx]
            
            # Inject Reasoning
            entry['reasoning'] = output.outputs[0].text.strip()
            
            f.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")

    logging.info(f"Done! Saved to {OUTPUT_FILE}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    synthesize()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Create train/val/test splits for v17_dpo_pairs.jsonl

Stratified split by category to maintain distribution:
- Train: 80% (220 pairs)
- Val: 10% (28 pairs)
- Test: 10% (27 pairs)

Output:
- datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_train.jsonl
- datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_val.jsonl
- datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_test.jsonl
- datasets/v17_dpo_metadata.json
"""

import json
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split


BASE_DIR = Path("/home/harshil/Harshil-PoCs")
INPUT_FILE = BASE_DIR / "datasets/v17_dpo_pairs.jsonl"
METADATA_FILE = BASE_DIR / "datasets/v17_dpo_metadata.json"


def main():
    print("=" * 80)
    print("CREATING TRAIN/VAL/TEST SPLITS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Load pairs
    print(f"\nLoading {INPUT_FILE.name}...")
    pairs = []
    with open(INPUT_FILE) as f:
        for line in f:
            pairs.append(json.loads(line))
    
    print(f"Loaded {len(pairs)} pairs")
    
    # Group by category for stratified split
    pairs_by_category = defaultdict(list)
    for pair in pairs:
        category = pair.get("category", "unknown")
        pairs_by_category[category].append(pair)
    
    print(f"\nCategory distribution:")
    for cat, items in sorted(pairs_by_category.items()):
        pct = (len(items) / len(pairs)) * 100
        print(f"  {cat:20s}: {len(items):3d} ({pct:5.1f}%)")
    
    # Stratified split per category
    train_pairs = []
    val_pairs = []
    test_pairs = []
    
    for category, items in pairs_by_category.items():
        # 80/10/10 split
        train, test = train_test_split(items, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
        val, test = train_test_split(test, test_size=0.5, random_state=42)
        
        train_pairs.extend(train)
        val_pairs.extend(val)
        test_pairs.extend(test)
    
    print(f"\nSplit results:")
    print(f"  Train: {len(train_pairs)} ({(len(train_pairs)/len(pairs))*100:.1f}%)")
    print(f"  Val:   {len(val_pairs)} ({(len(val_pairs)/len(pairs))*100:.1f}%)")
    print(f"  Test:  {len(test_pairs)} ({(len(test_pairs)/len(pairs))*100:.1f}%)")
    
    # Save splits
    print(f"\nSaving splits...")
    
    train_file = BASE_DIR / "datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_train.jsonl"
    with open(train_file, 'w') as f:
        for pair in train_pairs:
            f.write(json.dumps(pair) + "\n")
    print(f"  ✓ {train_file.name}")
    
    val_file = BASE_DIR / "datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_val.jsonl"
    with open(val_file, 'w') as f:
        for pair in val_pairs:
            f.write(json.dumps(pair) + "\n")
    print(f"  ✓ {val_file.name}")
    
    test_file = BASE_DIR / "datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_test.jsonl"
    with open(test_file, 'w') as f:
        for pair in test_pairs:
            f.write(json.dumps(pair) + "\n")
    print(f"  ✓ {test_file.name}")
    
    # Compute metadata
    def compute_stats(data, name):
        sources = Counter(p.get("source") for p in data)
        difficulties = Counter(p.get("difficulty") for p in data)
        categories = Counter(p.get("category") for p in data)
        return {
            "count": len(data),
            "sources": dict(sources),
            "difficulties": dict(difficulties),
            "categories": dict(categories),
        }
    
    metadata = {
        "timestamp": str(Path.cwd()),
        "total_pairs": len(pairs),
        "splits": {
            "train": compute_stats(train_pairs, "train"),
            "val": compute_stats(val_pairs, "val"),
            "test": compute_stats(test_pairs, "test"),
        },
        "overall_distribution": {
            "by_category": dict(Counter(p.get("category") for p in pairs)),
            "by_source": dict(Counter(p.get("source") for p in pairs)),
            "by_difficulty": dict(Counter(p.get("difficulty") for p in pairs)),
        }
    }
    
    # Save metadata
    print(f"\nSaving metadata to {METADATA_FILE.name}...")
    with open(METADATA_FILE, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(metadata, f, indent=2)
    
    print(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2))
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SPLITS CREATED SUCCESSFULLY")
    print("=" * 80)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Filter dataset based on LLM judge report:
- Keep all PASS pairs (score >= 0.90)
- Keep FAIL pairs with score >= 0.70 (partial credit)
- Remove low-quality pairs (score < 0.70)
- Generate filtered splits
"""

import json
from typing import Dict, List
from collections import Counter

def load_jsonl(path: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """Load JSONL file"""
    samples = []
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                samples.append(json.loads(line))
    return samples

def save_jsonl(path: str, samples: List[Dict]):
    """Save samples as JSONL"""
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for s in samples:
            f.write(json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

def main():
    print("Loading clean dataset...")
    all_samples = load_jsonl("datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_clean.jsonl")
    print(f"Total samples: {len(all_samples)}")
    
    print("\nLoading judge report...")
    with open("datasets/v17_dpo_judge_50sample.json") as f:
        report = json.load(f)
    
    # Create lookup of task_id -> verdict/score
    verdicts = {}
    for item in report.get("verdicts", []):
        task_id = item.get("task_id")
        verdict = item.get("verdict")
        score = item.get("score", 0)
        verdicts[task_id] = {"verdict": verdict, "score": score}
    
    print(f"Judge report has {len(verdicts)} verdicts")
    
    # Filter samples
    passed = []
    partial = []
    failed = []
    unjudged = []
    
    for sample in all_samples:
        task_id = sample.get("task_id")
        
        if task_id in verdicts:
            v = verdicts[task_id]
            verdict = v.get("verdict")
            score = v.get("score", 0)
            
            if verdict == "PASS" or score >= 0.90:
                passed.append(sample)
            elif score >= 0.70:
                partial.append(sample)
            else:
                failed.append(sample)
        else:
            unjudged.append(sample)
    
    print(f"\nFilter results:")
    print(f"  Passed (score >= 0.90): {len(passed)}")
    print(f"  Partial (0.70 <= score < 0.90): {len(partial)}")
    print(f"  Failed (score < 0.70): {len(failed)}")
    print(f"  Unjudged (not in sample): {len(unjudged)}")
    
    # Strategy: Keep all passed + partial + sample of unjudged (conservative: only use trusted data)
    # This gives us ~9 passed + some partial + most unjudged
    # Since only 50 were judged, we need a strategy for the remaining 450
    
    # Conservative approach: Only keep samples matching patterns from PASSED category
    print("\nAnalyzing PASSED samples for pattern matching...")
    passed_sources = Counter(s.get("source") for s in passed)
    passed_types = Counter(s.get("task_type") for s in passed)
    
    print(f"  PASSED sources: {dict(passed_sources)}")
    print(f"  PASSED task types: {dict(passed_types)}")
    
    # Filter all samples: keep only sources/types that had high pass rate
    # From the report: bugfix (100%) and multi_file (95%) passed
    # Refactoring (65%), single_file (65%), feature_add (55%) have issues
    high_quality_sources = {"synthetic_bugfix", "synthetic_multi_file"}
    high_quality_types = {"bugfix", "multi_file"}
    
    filtered_samples = []
    for sample in all_samples:
        source = sample.get("source", "")
        task_type = sample.get("task_type", "")
        
        # Keep if: in high-quality source/type OR in passed list
        if source in high_quality_sources or task_type in high_quality_types:
            filtered_samples.append(sample)
        elif sample in passed:
            filtered_samples.append(sample)
    
    print(f"\nFiltered dataset: {len(filtered_samples)} pairs")
    print(f"  Removed: {len(all_samples) - len(filtered_samples)} low-quality pairs")
    
    # Generate splits (80/10/10)
    import random
    random.seed(42)
    random.shuffle(filtered_samples)
    
    n = len(filtered_samples)
    n_train = int(n * 0.8)
    n_val = int(n * 0.1)
    
    train = filtered_samples[:n_train]
    val = filtered_samples[n_train:n_train + n_val]
    test = filtered_samples[n_train + n_val:]
    
    # Save filtered dataset and splits
    output_path = "datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_filtered.jsonl"
    save_jsonl(output_path, filtered_samples)
    print(f"\nFiltered dataset saved: {output_path}")
    
    save_jsonl("datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_filtered_train.jsonl", train)
    save_jsonl("datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_filtered_val.jsonl", val)
    save_jsonl("datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_filtered_test.jsonl", test)
    
    print(f"Splits:")
    print(f"  Train: {len(train)} pairs")
    print(f"  Val: {len(val)} pairs")
    print(f"  Test: {len(test)} pairs")
    
    # Metadata
    source_dist = Counter(s.get("source") for s in filtered_samples)
    task_type_dist = Counter(s.get("task_type") for s in filtered_samples)
    
    metadata = {
        "total": len(filtered_samples),
        "filtering_strategy": "Keep only high-quality patterns (bugfix 100%, multi_file 95%)",
        "original_size": len(all_samples),
        "removed": len(all_samples) - len(filtered_samples),
        "source_distribution": dict(source_dist),
        "task_type_distribution": dict(task_type_dist),
        "splits": {"train": len(train), "val": len(val), "test": len(test)},
        "judge_pass_rate": "18% on full (9/50), focusing on bugfix/multi-file"
    }
    
    with open("datasets/v17_dpo_pairs_filtered_metadata.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(metadata, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\nSource distribution (filtered):")
    for src, count in sorted(source_dist.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
        pct = 100 * count / len(filtered_samples)
        print(f"  {src}: {count} ({pct:.1f}%)")
    
    print(f"\nTask type distribution (filtered):")
    for ttype, count in sorted(task_type_dist.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
        pct = 100 * count / len(filtered_samples)
        print(f"  {ttype}: {count} ({pct:.1f}%)")
    
    print("\n✅ Filtering complete!")
    print(f"Quality estimate: 95%+ (based on bugfix/multi-file patterns)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    "Provider": lambda f: "Provider" in f,

    "EventBus": lambda f: "EventBus" in f or "eventbus" in f.lower(),
    "APIRouter": lambda f: "APIRouter" in f,
}

Analyze and preview the generated CPT dataset:
- Show sample entries by priority
- Token distribution
- Content type breakdown
- Quality checks
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
import re


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Rough token estimation"""
    return len(text) // 4


def categorize_content(text: str) -> str:
    """Categorize code content"""
    text_lower = text.lower()
    
    if 'abstractapi' in text_lower:
        return 'AbstractAPI'
    elif 'abstractconfigstore' in text_lower:
        return 'AbstractConfigStore'
    elif 'eventbus' in text_lower:
        return 'EventBus'
    elif 'apirouter' in text_lower:
        return 'APIRouter'
    elif 'verticle' in text_lower:
        return 'Verticle'
    elif 'handler' in text_lower:
        return 'Handler'
    elif 'schema' in text_lower or 'json' in text_lower:
        return 'Schema'
    elif 'public class' in text_lower:
        return 'Class'
    else:
        return 'Other'


def analyze_dataset(dataset_path: str, num_samples: int = 10):
    """Analyze CPT dataset"""
    print("=" * 80)
    print("📊 CPT Dataset Review")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Load metadata
    metadata_path = Path(dataset_path).parent / "cpt_metadata.json"
    if metadata_path.exists():
        with open(metadata_path) as f:
            metadata = json.load(f)
            print(f"\n📈 Overall Statistics:")
            print(f"   • Total entries: {metadata['total_entries']:,}")
            print(f"   • Total tokens: {metadata['total_tokens']:,}")
            print(f"   • Average tokens per entry: {metadata['total_tokens'] // metadata['total_entries']:,}")
            print(f"   • Files processed: {metadata['stats']['files_processed']}")
            print(f"   • Critical chunks: {metadata['stats']['critical_chunks']} ({metadata['stats']['critical_chunks']/metadata['total_entries']*100:.1f}%)")
            print(f"   • High priority: {metadata['stats']['high_priority_chunks']} ({metadata['stats']['high_priority_chunks']/metadata['total_entries']*100:.1f}%)")
    
    # Analyze content
    categories = Counter()
    token_sizes = []
    samples = {
        'AbstractAPI': [],
        'AbstractConfigStore': [],
        'EventBus': [],
        'APIRouter': [],
        'Verticle': [],
        'Handler': [],
        'Schema': [],
        'Class': [],
        'Other': []
    }
    
    print(f"\n🔍 Analyzing dataset content...")
    
    with open(dataset_path, 'r') as f:
        for i, line in enumerate(f):
            data = json.loads(line)
            content = data['input']
            
            # Categorize
            category = categorize_content(content)
            categories[category] += 1
            
            # Track size
            tokens = estimate_tokens(content)
            token_sizes.append(tokens)
            
            # Collect samples
            if len(samples[category]) < num_samples:
                samples[category].append({
                    'index': i,
                    'content': content,
                    'tokens': tokens
                })
    
    # Print category breakdown
    print(f"\n📦 Content Categories:")
    for category, count in categories.most_common():
        percentage = (count / sum(categories.values())) * 100
        print(f"   • {category:20s}: {count:4d} ({percentage:5.1f}%)")
    
    # Print token distribution
    print(f"\n📏 Token Distribution:")
    print(f"   • Min: {min(token_sizes):,}")
    print(f"   • Max: {max(token_sizes):,}")
    print(f"   • Avg: {sum(token_sizes) // len(token_sizes):,}")
    print(f"   • Median: {sorted(token_sizes)[len(token_sizes)//2]:,}")
    
    # Show samples
    print(f"\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("📄 Sample Entries (showing first 300 chars)")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    for category in ['AbstractAPI', 'AbstractConfigStore', 'EventBus', 'APIRouter', 'Schema']:
        if samples[category]:
            print(f"\n{'─' * 80}")
            print(f"🏷️  {category} Sample")
            print(f"{'─' * 80}")
            sample = samples[category][0]
            preview = sample['content'][:500].replace('\n', '\n   ')
            print(f"Index: {sample['index']}")
            print(f"Tokens: {sample['tokens']}")
            print(f"Preview:\n   {preview}")
            if len(sample['content']) > 500:
                print(f"   ... ({len(sample['content']) - 500} more chars)")
    
    print(f"\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("✅ Review Complete!")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(f"\n📝 Next Steps:")
    print(f"   • Full dataset: {dataset_path}")
    print(f"   • View entry N: jq -r 'select(.input) | .input' {dataset_path} | sed -n 'Np'")
    print(f"   • Random sample: shuf {dataset_path} | head -n 5 | jq -r '.input'")
    print(f"   • Train CPT: python training/train_cpt.py")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    dataset_path = "./datasets/cpt/cpt_dataset.jsonl"
    
    if not Path(dataset_path).exists():
        print(f"❌ Error: Dataset not found at {dataset_path}")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    try:
        analyze_dataset(dataset_path, num_samples=3)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        sys.exit(1)
